revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Festival Tickets
revealWordProblem.text:
Four friends are doing yard work around town to earn money for the Summer Music Festival advertised on the flyer. Tickets are $75.50 each. They charge $15 per hour for yard work and will combine their earnings.
Question: How many hours do the four friends need to work to earn enough money to buy four tickets? Propose a breakdown of how many hours each friend might work.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A Summer Music Festival flyer for August 5th and 6th at River Park Arena, priced at $75.50 per ticket.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Four tickets cost 4 × $75.50 = $302. At $15 an hour, write the inequality 15h ≥ 302, so h ≥ 302 ÷ 15 ≈ 20.13 hours. They cannot work part of an hour and come up short, so together they need at least 21 hours — which earns 21 × $15 = $315, enough with $13 left over. Split evenly that is 21 ÷ 4 = 5.25 hours each, so a workable breakdown is three friends working 5 hours and one working 6 hours.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do I write an inequality from words?
conceptIntro.intro: An inequality compares two amounts using <, >, ≤, or ≥. I use one when many values are allowed, not just one. I pick a variable and match the words to the right symbol. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 'At least' means ≥ and 'at most' means ≤; 'more than' means > and 'fewer/less than' means <.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Clue: 'The suspect is at least 18 years old.'
I let a stand for the age. 'At least 18' means 18 or more.
'At least' includes 18, so I use the symbol ≥.
My inequality is a ≥ 18. So a could be 18, 19, 20, and up.
linesEs: Pista: «El sospechoso tiene al menos 18 años.»
Dejo que a represente la edad. «Al menos 18» significa 18 o más.
«Al menos» incluye el 18, así que uso el símbolo ≥.
Mi desigualdad es a ≥ 18. Entonces a podría ser 18, 19, 20 y más.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Clue: 'A bag holds fewer than 10 items.' What does 'fewer than' mean?
It means less than, and it does NOT include 10, so we use <.
We let n be the number of items: n < 10.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."
linesEs: Pista: «Una bolsa lleva menos de 10 artículos.» ¿Qué significa «menos de»?
Significa menor que, y no incluye el 10, así que usamos <.
Dejamos que n sea el número de artículos: n < 10.
Marco de oración — dilo conmigo: «Mi primer paso es ___ , porque el problema pide ___ .»

linesEs: Intenta los problemas de práctica de abajo. El botón de pistas está ahí cuando te atores — úsalo, eso es ser listo.
Recuerda la idea clave: «Al menos» significa ≥ y «como máximo» significa ≤; «más de» significa > y «menos de» significa <.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Construyámoslo juntos — ¿Cómo escribo una desigualdad a partir de palabras?
conceptIntro.introEs: Una desigualdad compara dos cantidades usando <, >, ≤ o ≥. Uso una cuando se permiten muchos valores, no solo uno. Elijo una variable y hago corresponder las palabras con el símbolo correcto. Veremos un ejemplo resuelto, haremos uno juntos y luego harás algunos con pistas disponibles cuando las necesites.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: «Al menos» significa ≥ y «como máximo» significa ≤; «más de» significa > y «menos de» significa <.

diagram.instructions: Each graph shows one real-world rule. Write the inequality that matches the circle and the shading.

problems.label: The temperature is less than 40 degrees
You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride

hints: Open circle → the boundary is NOT included, so the symbol is < or >. Closed circle → the boundary IS included, so the symbol is ≤ or ≥.
Shaded to the right means the values are greater ( > or ≥ ). Shaded to the left means the values are less ( < or ≤ ).
'At least' means the boundary counts, so use ≥. 'More than' means it does not, so use >.

approaching.stem: Which inequality represents: 'The temperature is less than 40 degrees'?
approaching.explanation: 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
choiceFeedback: Your symbol opens toward temperatures ABOVE 40. 'Less than 40' lives on the other side — which way should the symbol point?
The ≤ symbol lets the temperature be exactly 40. 'Less than 40' leaves 40 out.
An equals sign pins the temperature to a single value, but this situation describes a whole range of temperatures.
hints: Find the comparison phrase: 'less than 40 degrees'. Does 40 itself count, or only temperatures below it?
'Less than' with no 'or equal to' means a strict symbol — no bar underneath — pointing toward the smaller side.
Test a value: is 35 degrees 'less than 40'? Yes — so pick the strict symbol that puts t on the smaller side of 40.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'La temperatura es menor que 40 grados'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Menor que' significa <, así que la desigualdad es t < 40.
hintsEs: Halla la frase de comparación: 'menos de 40 grados'. ¿Cuenta el 40 mismo o solo las temperaturas por debajo?
'Menos que' sin 'o igual a' significa un símbolo estricto —sin barra debajo— apuntando hacia el lado menor.
Prueba un valor: ¿35 grados es 'menos de 40'? Sí, así que elige el símbolo estricto que pone t del lado menor de 40.

approaching.stem: Which inequality represents: 'You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride'?
approaching.explanation: 'At least' means greater than or equal to, so h ≥ 48.
choiceFeedback: So close — test the boundary. Does a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall get to ride? Your strict symbol turns that rider away.
This describes riders who are too short to ride. Check which direction the symbol opens.
This would let anyone shorter than 48 inches ride. 'At least 48' makes 48 the smallest allowed height, not the largest.
hints: 'At least 48' — ask yourself: can a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall ride? That decides whether 48 is included.
When the boundary value is allowed, you need a symbol with the 'or equal to' bar under it.
Allowed heights are 48, 49, 50, and up. Pick the symbol that includes 48 itself AND points toward bigger numbers.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Debes medir al menos 48 pulgadas de estatura para subir'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Al menos' significa mayor que o igual a, así que h ≥ 48.
hintsEs: 'Al menos 48': pregúntate si alguien que mide EXACTAMENTE 48 pulgadas puede subir. Eso decide si el 48 se incluye.
Cuando el valor del límite sí se permite, necesitas un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual a' debajo.
Las estaturas permitidas son 48, 49, 50 y más. Elige el símbolo que incluya el 48 Y apunte hacia los números mayores.

approaching.stem: Which inequality represents: 'A store can hold no more than 75 people'?
approaching.explanation: 'No more than' means less than or equal to, so p ≤ 75.
choiceFeedback: Almost — check the boundary. Is a store holding EXACTLY 75 people breaking the rule? Your symbol says yes; re-read 'no more than.'
This says the store always holds 75 or more people, which is the opposite of a limit. 'No more than' caps the number.
This describes crowds larger than the limit. 'No more than 75' means the store never goes above 75.
hints: 'No more than 75' — could the store hold exactly 75 people? Could it hold 76?
'No more than' allows the boundary but nothing above it — that calls for a symbol with the 'or equal' bar.
Test values: 75 people is fine, 76 is not. Pick the symbol that keeps p at 75 or below.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Una tienda puede albergar no más de 75 personas'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'No más de' significa menor que o igual a, así que p ≤ 75.
hintsEs: 'No más de 75': ¿podría la tienda tener exactamente 75 personas? ¿Podría tener 76?
'No más de' permite el límite pero nada por encima: eso pide un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual'.
Prueba valores: 75 personas está bien, 76 no. Elige el símbolo que mantenga p en 75 o menos.

approaching.stem: Which inequality represents: 'The speed limit is more than 25 mph'?
approaching.explanation: 'More than' means strictly greater than, so s > 25.
choiceFeedback: Test the boundary value: is 25 itself 'more than 25'? Your symbol includes it — decide whether the words allow that.
The symbol points the wrong way. 'More than' describes speeds above 25, not below it.
An equals sign names one exact speed, but 'more than 25' covers every speed above 25.
hints: 'More than 25' — is exactly 25 included, or only speeds above 25?
'More than' (not 'at least') is strict — no 'or equal' bar under the symbol.
Test: 26 works, but 25 itself does not. Pick the strict symbol that puts s above 25.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'El límite de velocidad es más de 25 mph'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Más de' significa estrictamente mayor que, así que s > 25.
hintsEs: 'Más de 25': ¿se incluye exactamente 25 o solo las velocidades por encima de 25?
'Más de' (no 'al menos') es estricto: sin barra de 'o igual' debajo del símbolo.
Prueba: 26 sirve, pero 25 no. Elige el símbolo estricto que pone s por encima de 25.

approaching.instructions: Place markers on the number line for each value, then decide: is 5 > 3 true or false? Is 2 ≥ 7 true or false?
hints: On a number line, greater numbers are to the right. 5 is to the right of 3, so 5 > 3 is true.
2 is to the LEFT of 7, so 2 ≥ 7 is false.
approaching.explanation: On a number line the values grow as you move right, so a comparison is true when the first number sits to the right of the second. 5 lands to the right of 3, which makes 5 > 3 true, while 2 sits to the left of 7, so 2 ≥ 7 is false.
approaching.explanationEs: En una recta numérica los valores crecen conforme te mueves a la derecha, así que una comparación es verdadera cuando el primer número queda a la derecha del segundo. 5 cae a la derecha de 3, lo que hace que 5 > 3 sea verdadero, mientras que 2 queda a la izquierda de 7, así que 2 ≥ 7 es falso.
hintsEs: En una recta numérica, los números mayores están a la derecha. 5 está a la derecha de 3, así que 5 > 3 es verdadero.
2 está a la IZQUIERDA de 7, así que 2 ≥ 7 es falso.

rows.situation: A package weighs less than 50 pounds.
You need at least $25 to buy the game.
No more than 30 students can join the club.

approaching.label: Identify the key phrase, symbol, and write the inequality for each situation.
approaching.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Every row follows the same 3 steps: circle the key phrase, translate it into a symbol, then attach the variable and the number.
Remember: 'less than' is strict, while 'at least' and 'no more than' include the boundary — those two need the 'or equal' bar.
Row 1: the key phrase in 'weighs less than 50 pounds' is 'less than' — put its symbol between w and 50, then treat rows 2 and 3 the same way.
approaching.explanation: Every row uses the same three moves: find the key phrase, swap it for a symbol, then attach the variable and the number. "Less than" is strict, so the package row is w < 50, while "at least" and "no more than" both include their boundary, giving m ≥ 25 and s ≤ 30.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada fila usa los mismos tres pasos: encuentra la frase clave, cámbiala por un símbolo y luego une la variable con el número. "Menos de" es estricto, así que la fila del paquete es w < 50, mientras que "al menos" y "no más de" incluyen su límite, lo que da m ≥ 25 y s ≤ 30.
approaching.labelEs: Identifica la frase clave y el símbolo, y escribe la desigualdad de cada situación.
hintsEs: Cada fila sigue los mismos 3 pasos: encierra la frase clave, tradúcela a un símbolo y luego únele la variable y el número.
Recuerda: 'menos de' es estricto, mientras que 'al menos' y 'no más de' incluyen el límite; esos dos necesitan la barra de 'o igual'.
Fila 1: la frase clave en 'pesa menos de 50 libras' es 'menos de'; pon su símbolo entre w y 50, y trata las filas 2 y 3 igual.

onLevel.title: Spot the Detective's Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: The witness says the suspect is at least 16 years old.
workedExample.workEs: El testigo dice que el sospechoso tiene al menos 16 años.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let a stand for the suspect's age.
workedExample.workEs: Sea a la edad del sospechoso.

onLevel.correctWork: 'At least 16' means 16 itself counts as meeting the clue, plus any age older than 16. The symbol > would leave out exactly 16, so the correct inequality is a ≥ 16, not a > 16.
hints: Does 'at least 16' allow the suspect's age to be exactly 16, or must it be older?
'At least' means the boundary age itself satisfies the clue. Pick the symbol family that keeps 16 as a solution.
onLevel.explanation: The inequality step used >, which shuts out a suspect who is exactly 16. "At least 16" means 16 counts as well as every older age, so the clue is a ≥ 16 — the bar under the symbol is what lets the boundary age in.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la desigualdad usó >, lo que deja fuera a un sospechoso de exactamente 16 años. "Al menos 16" significa que 16 cuenta, igual que cualquier edad mayor, así que la pista es a ≥ 16: la barra debajo del símbolo es la que permite incluir la edad del límite.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 'Al menos 16' significa que 16 mismo cumple la pista, más cualquier edad mayor que 16. El símbolo > dejaría fuera exactamente el 16, así que la desigualdad correcta es a ≥ 16, no a > 16.
hintsEs: ¿'Al menos 16' permite que la edad del sospechoso sea exactamente 16, o debe ser mayor?
'Al menos' significa que el número de frontera también cumple la pista. Elige la familia de símbolos que mantiene el 16 como solución.

onLevel.stem: A parking garage charges if your stay is more than 2 hours. Which inequality represents times t that are charged?
onLevel.explanation: 'More than 2 hours' means strictly greater than: t > 2. Exactly 2 hours is not charged.
choiceFeedback: Think about the driver who stays exactly 2 hours. Your symbol charges them — does 'more than 2 hours' include exactly 2?
This describes short stays, which are not charged. Check which side of 2 the symbol opens toward.
This would charge a stay of exactly 2 hours, and it also covers shorter stays. 'More than 2' leaves 2 out and looks above it.
hints: The charge starts once the stay goes PAST 2 hours. Is a stay of exactly 2 hours charged?
If exactly 2 hours is NOT charged, the boundary is excluded — that rules out any symbol with the 'or equal' bar.
Test t = 2 and t = 3: only stays longer than 2 are charged. Pick the symbol that makes t = 3 true but t = 2 false.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estacionamiento cobra si tu estancia dura más de 2 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa los tiempos t que se cobran?
onLevel.explanationEs: 'Más de 2 horas' significa estrictamente mayor que: t > 2. Exactamente 2 horas no se cobra.
hintsEs: El cobro empieza cuando la estancia PASA de 2 horas. ¿Se cobra una estancia de exactamente 2 horas?
Si exactamente 2 horas NO se cobra, el límite queda excluido: eso descarta cualquier símbolo con la barra de 'o igual'.
Prueba t = 2 y t = 3: solo se cobran las estancias mayores de 2. Elige el símbolo que haga verdadero t = 3 y falso t = 2.

onLevel.title: Crack the Inequality Error

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: The report says no fewer than 9 witnesses saw the suspect.
workedExample.workEs: El informe dice que no menos de 9 testigos vieron al sospechoso.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let w stand for the number of witnesses.
workedExample.workEs: Sea w el número de testigos.

onLevel.correctWork: 'No fewer than 9' means the count cannot drop below 9 — 9 or more witnesses is required. That is w ≥ 9, not w < 9, which would only allow numbers below 9, the opposite of what the clue says.
hints: Does 'no fewer than 9' rule out having 9 witnesses, or does it rule out having fewer than 9?
'No fewer than 9' says 9 itself is acceptable — only counts BELOW 9 break the rule. Choose the symbol that keeps 9 in.
onLevel.titleEs: Resuelve el error de la desigualdad
onLevel.explanation: The inequality step pointed the symbol the wrong way. "No fewer than 9" means the count can never drop below 9, so 9 and every larger number works: w ≥ 9. The w < 9 that was written allows only counts under 9, which is the opposite of the clue.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la desigualdad apuntó el símbolo en la dirección equivocada. "No menos de 9" significa que el conteo nunca puede bajar de 9, así que sirven 9 y todos los números mayores: w ≥ 9. El w < 9 que se escribió solo permite conteos menores que 9, justo lo contrario de la pista.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 'No menos de 9' significa que el conteo no puede bajar de 9 — se requieren 9 testigos o más. Eso es w ≥ 9, no w < 9, que solo permitiría números por debajo de 9, lo contrario de lo que dice la pista.
hintsEs: ¿'No menos de 9' descarta tener 9 testigos, o descarta tener menos de 9?
'No menos de 9' dice que 9 en sí es aceptable — solo los conteos POR DEBAJO de 9 rompen la regla. Elige el símbolo que mantiene el 9 dentro.

onLevel.stem: A clue says the suspect carried at least 12 stolen gems. Which inequality shows the number g of gems?
onLevel.explanation: 'At least 12' includes 12 and any number above it, so g ≥ 12.
choiceFeedback: 'At least' includes 12 itself, so the symbol must allow equal to as well as greater than.
This allows fewer than 12 gems. 'At least 12' makes 12 the smallest possible number, not the largest.
This rules out 12 itself along with everything above it. 'At least' points the other way and includes the boundary.
onLevel.stemEs: Una pista dice que el sospechoso llevaba al menos 12 gemas robadas. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra el número g de gemas?
onLevel.explanationEs: 'Al menos 12' incluye el 12 y cualquier número mayor, así que g ≥ 12.
hints: An inequality has two things to decide: which direction it points, and whether the boundary number is included.
'At least 12' means 12 itself is allowed, so the symbol needs an 'or equal to' part.
Start with the boundary: 12 counts. Now decide whether the gem count goes above 12 or below it, and pick the matching symbol.
hintsEs: Una desigualdad tiene dos cosas que decidir: hacia dónde apunta y si el número del límite se incluye.
'Al menos 12' significa que el 12 sí se permite, así que el símbolo necesita la parte 'o igual a'.
Empieza con el límite: el 12 cuenta. Ahora decide si el número de gemas sube por encima de 12 o baja, y elige el símbolo que corresponde.

onLevel.stem: A witness reports that fewer than 5 people entered the building. Which inequality shows the number n of people?
onLevel.explanation: 'Fewer than 5' does not include 5, so n < 5.
choiceFeedback: 'Fewer than 5' does not include 5 itself, so equal to should not be allowed.
The symbol points the wrong way. 'Fewer than 5' describes counts below 5.
This includes 5 and everything above it. 'Fewer than 5' excludes 5 entirely.
onLevel.stemEs: Un testigo informa que menos de 5 personas entraron al edificio. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra el número n de personas?
onLevel.explanationEs: 'Menos de 5' no incluye el 5, así que n < 5.
hints: Decide two things: which way the inequality points, and whether 5 itself counts.
'Fewer than' excludes the boundary number, so no 'or equal to' part is needed.
5 is not allowed and the count has to stay below it. Write the symbol that says exactly that.
hintsEs: Decide dos cosas: hacia dónde apunta la desigualdad y si el 5 mismo cuenta.
'Menos de' excluye el número del límite, así que no hace falta la parte 'o igual a'.
El 5 no se permite y la cantidad debe quedarse por debajo. Escribe el símbolo que dice exactamente eso.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Catch the Symbol Mix-Up

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: The suspect is at least 12 years on the force, where y is the years.
workedExample.workEs: El sospechoso tiene al menos 12 años en el cuerpo, donde y son los años.

workedExample.label: Find the key phrase
workedExample.work: 'At least 12' means 12 is allowed and anything larger.
workedExample.workEs: 'Al menos 12' significa que 12 está permitido y cualquier cantidad mayor.

onLevel.correctWork: 'At least 12' includes 12 itself, so the symbol must be ≥, not >. Using > would leave out exactly 12 years. The correct inequality is y ≥ 12.
hints: Does 'at least 12' allow the value 12 itself, or only numbers bigger than 12?
'At least 12' keeps the boundary: check whether y = 12 satisfies your symbol before settling on strict or inclusive.
onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: atrapa la confusión de símbolos
onLevel.explanation: The inequality step used >, which shuts out a detective with exactly 12 years on the force. Because "at least 12" allows 12 itself along with anything larger, the symbol needs the bar underneath: y ≥ 12.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la desigualdad usó >, lo que deja fuera a un detective con exactamente 12 años de servicio. Como "al menos 12" permite el 12 mismo junto con cualquier número mayor, el símbolo necesita la barra debajo: y ≥ 12.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 'Al menos 12' incluye al propio 12, así que el símbolo debe ser ≥, no >. Usar > dejaría fuera exactamente los 12 años. La desigualdad correcta es y ≥ 12.
hintsEs: ¿'Al menos 12' permite el valor 12 en sí, o solo números mayores que 12?
'Al menos 12' conserva la frontera: comprueba si y = 12 satisface tu símbolo antes de decidir entre estricto e inclusivo.

onLevel.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: Which inequality represents: 'A store can hold no more than 75 people'?
workedExample.workEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Una tienda puede albergar no más de 75 personas'?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió

onLevel.correctWork: The correct answer is p ≤ 75. 'No more than' means less than or equal to, so p ≤ 75.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es p ≤ 75. 'No más de' significa menor que o igual a, así que p ≤ 75.
hints: 'No more than 75' — could the store hold exactly 75 people? Could it hold 76?
hintsEs: 'No más de 75': ¿podría la tienda tener exactamente 75 personas? ¿Podría tener 76?

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Write Inequalities is using a strict symbol (> or <) for a phrase that actually includes the boundary value. For 'the suspect is at least 18 years old,' students often write a > 18 instead of the correct a ≥ 18 — this wrongly excludes 18 itself, even though 'at least 18' means 18 counts as a match. The same error happens in reverse with 'at most': for 'the getaway bag holds at most 12 items,' students write n < 12 instead of n ≤ 12. Always ask: does the key phrase include the number ('at least,' 'at most,' 'no more than,' 'no fewer than' → use ≥ or ≤) or exclude it ('more than,' 'fewer than' → use > or <)?

connect.scenario: A detective knows the getaway car was traveling at most 65 miles per hour on the highway. The inequality s ≤ 65 represents the car's speed s.
connect.promptQuestion: What speeds are possible for the getaway car? How did the phrase 'at most' help you write the inequality?
connect.prompt: A speed of 65 mph is ___, a speed of 70 mph is ___, because 'at most 65' means the speed must be ___ 65.

check.stem: Which speed is NOT possible for the getaway car?
check.explanation: 'At most 65' means the speed is 65 or lower. 70 is above 65, so it is not possible. 65 itself IS allowed.
check.stemEs: ¿Qué velocidad no es posible para el carro de huida?
check.explanationEs: «Como máximo 65» significa que la velocidad es 65 o menos. 70 está por encima de 65, así que no es posible. El 65 mismo sí se permite.

choices: No — it must be strictly less
Yes — the 'or equal to' part includes 65
check.explanation: The ≤ symbol means 'less than OR equal to', so 65 is a solution.
check.explanationEs: El símbolo ≤ significa «menor que o igual a», así que el 65 es una solución.
choicesEs: Sí — la parte de «o igual a» incluye el 65
Solo si el carro se detiene

check.explanation: 'At most' sets a ceiling that can be reached: s ≤ 65. 'Fewer than' or 'under' would be s < 65.
check.explanationEs: «Como máximo» pone un techo que sí se puede alcanzar: s ≤ 65. «Menos de» o «por debajo de» sería s < 65.

connect.modelAnswer: 'At most 65' means the speed is less than or equal to 65, written s ≤ 65. So 65, 60, 45 and every value below 65 are possible — but 70 is not. The 'or equal to' part matters: 65 itself is allowed.
connect.promptEs: Una velocidad de 65 mph es ___, una velocidad de 70 mph es ___, porque «como máximo 65» significa que la velocidad debe ser ___ 65.
connect.scenarioEs: Una detective sabe que el carro de huida iba como máximo a 65 millas por hora en la carretera. La desigualdad s ≤ 65 representa la velocidad s del carro.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Qué velocidades son posibles para el carro de huida? ¿Cómo te ayudó la frase «como máximo» a escribir la desigualdad?
connect.modelAnswerEs: «Como máximo 65» significa que la velocidad es menor que o igual a 65, escrito s ≤ 65. Así que 65, 60, 45 y todos los valores por debajo de 65 son posibles — pero 70 no. La parte de «o igual a» importa: el 65 mismo se permite.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Which inequality represents: 'A number n is at least 14'?
exitTicket.explanation: 'At least 14' means 14 or greater, so n ≥ 14.
choiceFeedback: 'At least' includes 14 — you need the 'or equal to' line.
'At least' means 14 or more, so the arrow points the other way.
'At least 14' means 14 or greater, not less than.
hints: 'At least 14' — ask first: does 14 itself count as a solution?
If 14 counts, you need the symbol with the 'or equal' bar that also points toward larger numbers.
Test n = 14 and n = 20 (both should work) and n = 10 (should fail). Pick the symbol that passes all three tests.
exitTicket.stemEs: Revisión rápida — tú puedes: ¿Qué desigualdad representa «Un número n es al menos 14»?
exitTicket.explanationEs: «Al menos 14» significa 14 o más, así que n ≥ 14.
choiceFeedbackEs: «Al menos» incluye el 14 — necesitas la línea de «o igual a».
«Al menos» significa 14 o más, así que la flecha apunta al otro lado.
«Al menos 14» significa 14 o más, no menos que 14.
hintsEs: «Al menos 14» — pregunta primero: ¿el 14 mismo cuenta como solución?
Si el 14 cuenta, necesitas el símbolo con la barra de «o igual» que además apunta hacia los números más grandes.
Prueba n = 14 y n = 20 (los dos deben funcionar) y n = 10 (debe fallar). Escoge el símbolo que pase las tres pruebas.

questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 6 × 7 = 42 ✓
questions.explanationEs: Divide los dos lados entre 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Comprueba: 6 × 7 = 42 ✓
choiceFeedback: That's close, but check the division again — it isn't quite right.
That adds 6 to 42 instead of undoing the multiplication.
That multiplies 42 by 6 instead of dividing by it.
choiceFeedbackEs: Está cerca, pero revisa otra vez la división — no es del todo correcta.
Eso suma 6 a 42 en lugar de deshacer la multiplicación.
Eso multiplica 42 por 6 en lugar de dividir entre 6.

questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 3: n = 8 × 3 = 24. Check: 24 / 3 = 8 ✓
questions.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos lados por 3: n = 8 × 3 = 24. Comprueba: 24 / 3 = 8 ✓
choiceFeedback: That's the number already in the equation, not the value of n that makes it true.
That divides again instead of multiplying to undo the division.
That subtracts 3 from 8 instead of undoing the division.
choiceFeedbackEs: Ese es el número que ya está en la ecuación, no el valor de n que la hace verdadera.
Eso divide otra vez en lugar de multiplicar para deshacer la división.
Eso resta 3 de 8 en lugar de deshacer la división.

choiceFeedback: That subtracts 9 from 63 instead of dividing by 9.
That adds 9 to 63 instead of undoing the multiplication.
That multiplies 63 by 9 instead of dividing by it.
choiceFeedbackEs: Eso resta 9 de 63 en lugar de dividir entre 9.
